newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies ITT motion to dismiss law firm.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies ITT motion to dismiss law firm.

text.p: A federal district judge has denied an ITT Corp motion that would have required Hilton Hotels Corp to discharge law firm Latham & Watkins in the companies' struggle for control of ITT.

Late last week, District Judge Philip Pro ruled "ITT has failed to present evidence of an ethical violation by Latham & Watkins or a basis for enjoining Hilton from utilizing the services of Latham & Watkins."
Hilton filed Judge Pro's ruling with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday.
An ITT spokesman declined to comment.
In January, Hilton launched a $6.5 billion hostile bid for ITT, which ITT called inadeqate. The companies have several legal claims pending in U.S. District Court in Nevada.
In one ITT counterclaim filed on February 13, ITT alleged that Hilton had access to confidential information because Latham & Watkins had been hired by ITT in the past.
ITT claimed that if Hilton used the information, "ITT and its stockholders will be irreparably injured," according to ITT's counterclaim.
